daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

PKS announced it will communicate with other DPR factions regarding the controversy over Vice President Gibran's educational credentials. During a Constitutional Court hearing on the Election Law, PKS politician Arsul Sani raised the issue of a regional election candidate holding a master's degree but not graduating from high school. The controversy has prompted an alumni of Universitas Sebelas Maret to file a petition at the Constitutional Court challenging the requirement for high school diploma proof for presidential and vice-presidential candidates.

  • The Cabinet Secretary's office presented a performance report on two years of the Prabowo-Gibran administration, while Gerindra party highlighted achievements including the free meal program and People's Schools.
  • Golkar Party chairman Bahlil stated that party leaders who give too many speeches will not attract Generation Z voters, and addressed speculation about his chances of becoming Prabowo's running mate by referencing Golkar's history.
  • Bahlil also commented on the case of Nusron Wahid, who has twice failed to appear for KPK questioning.
  • Alumni of the Presidential Advisory Council raised concerns about a Constitutional Court petition seeking to limit the number of Wantimpres members to nine.
  • Student groups including BEM UI held demonstrations at Tugu Tani marking two years of the Prabowo-Gibran government, using the three-finger symbol as a sign of resistance.
  • Greenpeace activists unfurled protest banners about disasters at the Bundaran HI monument, and police are examining CCTV footage to determine how six activists climbed the monument.
  • Former Central Java Governor Ganjar Pranowo urged President Prabowo to declare the forest and land fires a national disaster.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia's Ambassador to Saudi Arabia urged state shipbuilder PT PAL to tap into the Middle East market for potential defence and commercial contracts. Meanwhile, five territorial military commands (Kodim) in Central Java transferred command to Kodam Mataram, representing a significant restructuring of regional military organization.

  • The European Union allocated US$224,500 in aid to help Indonesia tackle drought conditions.
  • The Indonesian government responded to Greenpeace protests concerning climate change and living costs.

Other

The Corruption Eradication Commission (KPK) seized Rp 250 million from the Nias branch of Nahdlatul Ulama (PCNU) in connection with a corruption case at the Ministry of Agrarian Affairs and Spatial Planning (ATR/BPN). Attorney General disclosed that only 10 percent at most of assets are typically recovered for crime victims. The Deputy Attorney General also emphasized that military justice must be based on actions, responding to a Constitutional Court ruling.

  • The Ministry of Finance denied reports that civil servant salaries would be distributed through village cooperatives, confirming payments will continue through banks.
  • BRIN confirmed that mysterious metal debris found in a Central Kalimantan palm oil plantation was Chinese rocket waste.
  • Police reported that 33 forest fire cases in West Kalimantan involved corporations, while authorities extinguished 454 hectares of land fires in key regions.
  • Police are investigating possible negligence or sabotage in the Batam-Bintan blackout.
  • President Prabowo will launch the National Digital Social Protection platform on Heroes' Day, November 10, 2026.
